subject: chemistry
title: Enthalpy Comet: ΔH and Hess Cycles
welcome_lead: Trace the energy flow of reactions using enthalpy and Hess's law.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on enthalpy changes and Hess cycles.
final_note: You have mastered energy bookkeeping in reactions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
To find ΔHr from ΔHf values: ΔHr = Σ ΔHf(products) - Σ ΔHf(reactants).

To find ΔHr from ΔHc values: ΔHr = Σ ΔHc(reactants) - Σ ΔHc(products). Always include states and multiply by stoichiometric coefficients.

ΔH ≈ Σ bonds broken - Σ bonds made. Bonds broken = endothermic (+), bonds made = exothermic (-).

Bond enthalpies are mean values, so this gives only an estimate. Works only when all species are gaseous.

q = m c ΔT. For solutions take m as the solution mass and c as 4.18 J/g/K.

ΔH per mol = -q / n (negative because exothermic releases heat to surroundings). Heat loss to surroundings makes measured values less exothermic than true.
